title: REBOA In Bleeding and Cardiac Arrest in the Pre-hospital care by Helicopter Emergency Medical Service. The RIPCAP-HEMS feasibility study.
summary: Patients with life-threatening internal bleeding or cardiac arrest represent a very critical group of patients. With the current standard care of this critical group of patients, some of these patients die before they reach the hospital. Internal clamping of the aorta using REBOA could save some of these patients. The aim of this study is to investigate whether the REBOA procedure can be used safely and effectively in the prehospital care setting.
conditions: Fracture of lumbar spine and pelvis
Traumatic amputation of hip and thigh

interventions.name: Accompanying scientific documentation of the introduction of the prehospital invasive procedure for occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) in life-threatening abdominal and pelvic bleeding and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and outcome analysis after inpatient discharge.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Trauma
-NACA-Score >=4
-BP<90mmHg,
HR> 120/min or <50/min
-Suspected NCTH

Non traumatic OHCA
-time to BLS <10 minutes
- high quality ACLS for at least 10 minutes without ROSC
Exclusion criteria:
Trauma 
-stable patient
-non compressible supradiaphracmatic bleeding
-injuries with no chance of survival 

OHCA
Age >76years
-Unwitnessed cardiac arrest or time to BLS > 10 minutes
-DNR order
- kwon terminal malignant underlying disease
-massive care dependency
